description: A hierarchical inference engine for frontier MoE models: hot experts on the GPU (CUDA, Vulkan), warm ones in RAM, cold ones streamed from NVMe. Written in C, runs on the hardware you already own.

summary.one_liner: colibri is a pure-C inference engine that runs very large mixture-of-experts language models (and a few image and decision models) on ordinary hardware by keeping hot experts on GPU or RAM and streaming cold experts from disk.
keywords: run huge model on small ram
use_cases: run a very large open MoE model on a PC with limited RAM
serve a local OpenAI or Anthropic compatible API for coding tools
chat with a local model in the terminal or a browser dashboard
answer yes/no or multiple-choice decisions from a document with probabilities
run GGUF model files from Hugging Face without converting them
benchmark and tune LLM inference across CPU, Vulkan and CUDA
how_to_run: Windows: download the ZIP and double-click START-HERE.bat
sudo apt install git python3 build-essential
git clone the repository, cd colibri, ./start-here.sh
macOS: xcode-select --install; brew install libomp git python; then ./start-here.sh
Manual: cd colibri/c && ./setup.sh && make qwen36 VK=1
notable: Hierarchical placement: hot experts in VRAM, warm in RAM, cold streamed from disk, with a learned usage cache
Runs GGUF files as published (IQ1_S to Q8_0, F16, BF16, MXFP4) via coli import
System One endpoint returns probabilities over allowed options instead of free text
OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic-compatible and Jev-compatible APIs from one server
Guided one-step setup that detects hardware, recommends a model and builds for the GPU
caveats: Very large models run slowly when experts stream from disk (for example 0.05-0.1 tok/s for GLM-5.2 on a 25 GB laptop)
Needs substantial disk space: 22 GB for the smallest model, up to 1.56 TB for Kimi K3
Some models need a manual conversion or preparation step, and some GPU paths depend on the CUDA toolkit version or card generation
